# ngx-request-lock

> Angular library that binds UI flows to HTTP request lifecycles. A shared `requestId` coordinates buttons, forms and panels across single or chained requests, unlocking them together when the flow settles, without manual `loading` flags. Requires Angular 22+, standalone APIs, functional HTTP interceptors and signals. MIT licensed.

## Docs

- [Home](https://ngx-request-lock-docs.netlify.app/): Overview, install command and entry points to the guides.
- [Problem statement](https://ngx-request-lock-docs.netlify.app/problem/): Why unblocked UI causes duplicate HTTP requests and stale loading flags, and how a shared requestId fixes it.
- [Architecture](https://ngx-request-lock-docs.netlify.app/architecture/): How the directive, HttpContext, interceptor and reference-counted signal service connect.
- [Installation and setup](https://ngx-request-lock-docs.netlify.app/installation/): Add provideRequestLock() or register the interceptor manually.
- [Directive usage](https://ngx-request-lock-docs.netlify.app/directive-usage/): Per-element patterns: basic, CRUD, pending state, custom directive.
- [Flow lock examples](https://ngx-request-lock-docs.netlify.app/flow-lock/): One requestId coordinating a whole flow of chained requests.

- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ngx-request-lock): Published library.
